title: Nonasymptotic Confidence Intervals for Rare Exposure Effects in Bernoulli Network Experiments
banked_reason: Math review PASS and positioning review PASS, but the independent novelty tier was subfield below the requested field floor.
gap_reasons: Novelty tier: subfield < requested field floor.
The general fractional-color Bernstein interval is established supporting machinery, not the novelty claim.
Unequal-block/conventional-alpha salvage requires genuinely new heterogeneous interval and weighted lower-bound research absent from the live package.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the finite-sample exposure-HT concentration result and a moderate-deviation clique-block same-class confidence-length sandwich whose effective count is n/(r 2^r). Independent math and positioning reviews passed, but novelty review placed the contribution at subfield rather than the requested field tier because the general upper interval is established substrate. A field-tier successor would need a genuinely new heterogeneous-network interval and matching weighted lower bound, rather than another refinement of this block witness.
tldr: For design-based exposure effects under Bernoulli network experiments, the paper pairs a computable fractional-chromatic Bernstein interval, valid over the full nonhomogeneous exposure class, with an exact homogeneous-witness transport that attains the effective rare-exposure count and yields a same-class expected-length sandwich; the concentration mechanism itself is established substrate, not the novelty claim.
gap: The unresolved comparison is confidence-interval length for rare network exposures, not the existence of exposure-HT or dependency-graph concentration. Aronow--Samii provides the design-based exposure framework, exposure-HT estimation, and variance-based interference inference, but not this expected-length lower bound or same-class sandwich. Pelekis--Ramon--Wang provides the exact-fold Holder aggregation used on the upper side, and Janson (2004, Theorem 2.3) provides generic fractional-chromatic Bernstein-type large deviations for bounded partly dependent sums in terms of \(\chi^*\), summed variances, and a summand bound; neither supplies an exposure-HT causal interval, an e-value, the exact rare-revelation reduction, or the confidence-length comparison. Sandoval--Balakrishnan--Feller--Jordan--Waudby-Smith assumes SUTVA and ordinary direct two-arm outcomes under Bernoulli or complete randomization and proves information-theoretic minimax RMSE rates of order \(1/\sqrt{n\pi}\), rather than uniformly valid interval expected-length lower bounds carrying \(\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}\); it has neither network-exposure modeling nor the exact transport to independent rare reveals, although its effective-count intuition is consistent with \(B=n/r\), \(q=2^{-r}\), and rate \(1/\sqrt{Bq}\) after the present homogeneous-witness reduction. Leung (2022) studies approximate neighborhood interference and asymptotic inference; Harshaw--Middleton--Savje (2026) optimizes variance estimation under interference and complex designs; Ham et al. (2022) develops design-based confidence sequences; Kandiros et al. (2024) studies conflict-graph design and estimation under arbitrary neighborhood interference; Tchetgen Tchetgen--VanderWeele gives partial-interference benchmarks, including finite-sample concentration-based inference; and Rigdon--Hudgens gives exact binary-outcome intervals under two-stage partial interference. None of those results establishes the present fixed-confidence, balanced-Bernoulli clique-block, rare-exposure expected-length lower bound and attained same-class comparison. The scope distinction is essential: upper validity is over the larger nonhomogeneous clique-block class, whereas exact compression and the lower bound use only the homogeneous witness subclass.
fill: The paper fills that niche by transporting a block-homogeneous witness exactly to independent rare revelations and using it to certify the lower endpoint of an attained expected-length sandwich, while the fractional-color interval supplies the upper endpoint over the larger nonhomogeneous clique-block class. The lower witness is a subclass argument: upper validity is genuinely nonhomogeneous, whereas exact compression and the lower bound use only homogeneous target schedules. Relative to Aronow--Samii, the added object is the lower bound and same-class comparison, not the exposure-HT framework. Relative to Pelekis--Ramon--Wang and Janson (2004, Theorem 2.3), the addition is the causal specialization together with exact witness transport and decision-theoretic interval-length analysis, not Holder or fractional-chromatic Bernstein concentration. Relative to Sandoval--Balakrishnan--Feller--Jordan--Waudby-Smith, the result is aligned with effective count \(Bq\) but is not a corollary because their SUTVA RMSE theorems do not furnish network-exposure interval-length risk or its \(\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}\) dependence. Relative to Leung, Harshaw--Middleton--Savje, Ham et al., Kandiros et al., Tchetgen Tchetgen--VanderWeele, and Rigdon--Hudgens, it adds the fixed balanced-Bernoulli rare-exposure lower-bound transport and same-class sandwich, rather than asymptotic approximate-interference inference, optimal variance estimation, confidence sequences, conflict-graph design, partial-interference concentration alone, or exact two-stage binary intervals.
